title: prefill-decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage overlap scheduling
author: Marco Chen
description: Motivation: prefilling the KV cache and decoding are currently executed as strictly sequential stages which increases tail latency for short/interactive requests and prevents early token streaming. This PR implements a chunked prefill path combined with speculative prefill and stage overlap scheduling so that decode can start earlier while the remainder of the prefill continues in the background. The approach reduces end-to-end p95 latency on small prompts and improves token throughput for typical PLG workloads without sacrificing correctness. Summary of changes: 1) Chunked prefill: split long prefill streams into contiguous chunks that can be decoded incrementally and merged into KV cache. 2) Speculative prefill path: launch prefill work ahead-of-time for compatible models when sequence length heuristics indicate benefit, with safe rollback if mismatch detected. 3) Stage overlap scheduler: new lightweight scheduler that allows decode workers to consume available KV cache state produced by earlier prefill chunks while remaining prefill chunks continue on other workers. 4) Kernel selection tweaks: minor heuristics to prefer attention kernels that have low setup cost when operating on chunked inputs. 5) KV cache concurrency fixes: introduced fine-grained guards and epoch checks to avoid race conditions when speculative prefill is rolled back. 6) Continuous batching adjustments: batching window logic updated to account for chunk boundaries and speculative prefill traffic. Design notes: chunk sizes are adaptive based on model type, sequence length and current batch sizes; speculative prefill is gated by a confidence heuristic derived from recent request distributions and model compatibility table; overlap scheduling uses per-request stage tokens to decide when decode can safely start. Safety: invariant checks ensure decode only reads KV entries that are fully initialized for the required timestep; speculative prefill that gets invalidated triggers a small decode stall and replay path but not a silent corruption. Testing and validation: added microbenchmarks and e2e benchmark harness runs; unit tests for KV cache races and epoching; integration tests for streaming correctness. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag "chunked_speculative_prefill" and enabled for Canary fleet for 2 weeks before broad rollout. See linked Linear tickets for rollout tracking.

benchmarks_summary: Short prompts (<=64 tokens), batch=1: end-to-end p95 latency reduced by 22% (from 120ms to 94ms) on A100; median latency reduced by 16%
Medium prompts (65-256 tokens), batch=4: p95 reduced by 11%, throughput (tokens/s) unchanged or slightly improved
Long prompts (>256 tokens): negligible change or small regression (<3%) depending on chunking heuristics
Token throughput: +12% measured on A100 microbench for decode-dominant workloads due to earlier decode start
Speculative prefill acceptance rate: 78% on canary traces; rollback path latency penalty observed in 22% of speculative attempts but within SLO
release_notes: Runtime: prefilling and decode stages can now overlap. Adds a feature flag 'chunked_speculative_prefill' that enables chunked prefill, speculative prefill and stage-overlap scheduling. Improves short-request tail latency and token throughput. Enabled for canary by default; opt-in for broader rollout.
